Additionally, a multi-head Aspect-aware attention network independently extracts features from local and global contexts. Pretrained BERT models enhance performance. Experiments on Twitter, Laptop, and Restaurant datasets, evaluated using Accuracy and Fl-score, demonstrate that our model outperforms other aspect-based sentiment classification algorithms with a more compact parameter size.

articleTitle: Research and Implementation of Drug Relocation Algorithm Based on Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Computer and Automation Engineering (ICCAE)
abstract: Traditional drug development involves expensive and time-consuming high-throughput screening experiments to assess the interaction between drug molecules and target proteins. Given the vast number of potential compounds and targets, comprehensive screening is impractical. Therefore, researchers have turned to deep learning methods for predicting drug molecule-target protein binding affinity. A novel approach is proposed, utilizing graph isomorphism networks and multi-scale convolutional neural networks in an end-to-end model. This model employs a Siamese architecture to separately extract features from drug molecules and target proteins. Additionally, it incorporates an attention mechanism to focus on crucial elements. Finally, the feature vectors are concatenated and used for affinity prediction. Experimental results on the Davis and KIBA benchmark datasets demonstrate the model's strong performance in predicting drug molecule-target protein binding affinity.

articleTitle: Hierarchical Tracking Control for a Composite Mobile Robot Considering System Uncertainties
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Computer and Automation Engineering (ICCAE)
abstract: Composite mobile robots (CMRs) have gained extensive application in the industrial sector due to their integrated loading and operational capabilities. The trajectory tracking control module, being a vital constituent, directly influences the degree of stability in robot operations. However, current tracking control methods exhibit suboptimal performance when encountering system uncertainties arising from both the environment and inherent system factors. This paper presents a novel hierarchical control strategy tailored for the hierarchical model of composite mobile robot chassis. This strategy effectively combines velocity control and torque control, resulting in satisfactory trajectory tracking control. Firstly, a hierarchical kinematic and dynamic model is constructed to account for varying payload and environmental uncertainties. Subsequently, a pose-velocity-torque hierarchical controller is formulated to regulate chassis speed by manipulating torque input, thereby achieving pose regulation and trajectory tracking. Finally, the control algorithm is implemented using MATLAB and adapted to industrial computers for the development and validation of the controller's effectiveness. Comparative experiments are conducted against existing methods, demonstrating the superiority of the proposed controller.

articleTitle: ERSA-Net:Encoder Networks based on Residuals and Self-Attention for Accelerating MRI Reconstruction
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Computer and Automation Engineering (ICCAE)
abstract: Accelerating magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) reconstruction with deep learning-based methods is a challenging task. This paper proposes ERSA-Net, an encoder-based residual self-attention network for MRI reconstruction. This network is designed to reconstruct high-quality magnetic resonance images from undersampled K-space data. In particular, the backbone network architecture we propose is based on an encoder. It employs a series of residual blocks to improve the utilization of feature information in each encoder layer. As each layer progresses, we always use a residual network to retain feature information in each layer. In addition, the proposed ERSA-Net utilizes a specialized feature extractor to extract important feature values. It then performs self-attention calculations on the extracted information to identify dependencies between feature values and enhance the performance of the network model. We validated the effectiveness of ERSA - N et on datasets with various undersampling ratios and demonstrated that it significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods.

articleTitle: Long-Term Load Forecasting for Luzon, Philippines using Optimized Hybrid Machine Learning Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Computer and Automation Engineering (ICCAE)
abstract: This research paper discusses the growing demand for electricity in the Philippines due to population growth, economic development, and the need for accurate long-term electrical load forecasting to sustain the power system since most load forecasting studies focus on short-term duration. The study aims to optimize, evaluate, and compare accurate load forecasting models for the load demand of Luzon. This study used machine learning techniques for forecasting, specifically Linear Support Vector Machine (Linear SVM), Multi-layer Perceptron (MLP), and Linear Regression with XGBoost (LR-XGBoost). The objectives include identifying and constructing relevant features, optimizing hyperparameters, and comparing performances using appropriate evaluation metrics. The study is significant to the power system industry. Electrical load forecasting equipped them to create operational decisions in energy management, generation scheduling, and assessment that maintain supply and demand. The comparison will solely focus on the three models and identify how the models performed using the Luzon hourly load demand from 2013 to 2022. Based on the results, the optimized LR-XGboost is the best-performing Long- Term Load Forecasting Model for the Load Demand of Luzon with a MAPE of 4.61 %, outperforming the optimized Linear SVR and MLP models. The researchers recommend adding external regressors such as historical weather and economic data, performing Scenario forecasting, and adding holiday indicators to improve the performance of each model.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Based Trajectory Prediction in Autonomous Driving Tasks: A Survey
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Computer and Automation Engineering (ICCAE)
abstract: Nowadays, autonomous driving technology has greatly advanced. Trajectory prediction, as a significant part of autonomous driving, is highly valued because it serves as a connecting link between the tracking module and the planning module. Therefore, it is of great value to review the existing trajectory prediction methods and summarize their advantages and disadvantages. This paper provides a thorough review of trajectory prediction methods. Specifically, based on the types of input information, we classify trajectory prediction methods into those using temporal information only and those combining both temporal and spatial information. For each category, we comprehensively introduce specific methods along with associated challenges, shortcomings, and research gaps. Finally, we summarize the advantages and disadvantages of these methods and compare their performance on public datasets for future research in trajectory prediction.

articleTitle: An optimal UAV and UGV Cooperative Network Navigation Algorithm for Bushfire Surveillance and Disaster Relief
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Computer and Automation Engineering (ICCAE)
abstract: In addressing the challenges of rapid bushfire evacuation, this paper presents an integrated air-ground autonomous system harnessing both Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) and Unmanned Ground Vehicles(UGV). Drawing inspiration from prior works, our approach employs UAVs for disaster area surveillance using Coverage Path Planning (CPP) to comprehensively assess fire dynamics. Upon detecting fire in high-risk zones, the UAV not only alerts the nearby residents but also formulates an evacuation path to safe zones. Concurrently, unmanned vehicles, guided by these UAVs and leveraging the reactive algorithm, are dispatched for victim retrieval, ensuring efficient navigation around obstacles. This dual-system response is framed as an optimization problem. This approach melds advanced fire modeling with state-of-the-art navigation for an improved bushfire response strategy.

articleTitle: A Distributed and Self-powered Soil Monitoring Network for Smart Agriculture
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Computer and Automation Engineering (ICCAE)
abstract: Real-time soil fertility monitoring can help evaluate soil quality in time for soil improvement, which in turn improves agricultural yields. This paper presents a self-powered and distributed soil monitoring network for smart farms. Each monitoring node is powered by a battery <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(5000\ mAh)$</tex> and a small photovoltaic panel to continuously charge the battery, which enables the monitoring nodes to be widely distributed in the farm and continuously monitor soil data with soil fertility parameters, such as nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium, pH, moisture and temperature. All monitoring data can be transferred to a remote data server in the cloud via a 4G/5G network and MQTT protocol. This allows users to analyse the soil monitoring data via an APP to support further operational decisions, such as watering or fertilising. To minimise power consumption and maximise the duration of the power supply, a power management circuit is designed to support the sleep mode, which can turn off the sensors and 4G module during the sleeping period and turn them back on for data monitoring and transmission. Experimental results show that even without charging from the photovoltaic panel, the battery can support the continuous operation of the monitoring node for about eight days, which means that the designed system can be widely used in wild farms for long-term soil monitoring.

articleTitle: Possibilities of Using Deep Convolutional Neural Network and Autoencoder Neural Network for Predictive Maintenance Tasks
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Computer and Automation Engineering (ICCAE)
abstract: Entering the era of Industry 4.0, artificial intelligence has also found a place in the manufacturing industry. In the last decade, there has been an increased interest in the topic of AI in manufacturing. The issues of maintenance and technical diagnostics are significantly linked to the issues of manufacturing and represent a significant area of interest for science and research. Maintenance has so far been associated with modern technologies and analytical methods. Greater emphasis is being placed on predictive maintenance models that use operational data on the current state of machinery and equipment, allowing potential problems in systems to be identified before failure or malfunction occurs. This issue is one of the basic parts of any production process and is an indication of the malfunctioning and faulty states of production systems. For these reasons, the present research deals with the analysis of the possibilities of using deep convolutional neural networks and autoencoder networks for the tasks of signal processing, prediction of operating parameters, and anomaly detection in hydraulic circuits.

articleTitle: Metaverse Ecosystem Realization for its Application Development
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Computer and Automation Engineering (ICCAE)
abstract: The concept of the metaverse, a seamlessly integrated virtual universe, has gained substantial traction in recent years. It delves into the technological foundations, socioeconomic implications, and user experience paradigms that underpin the Metaverse, emphasizing its potential to revolutionize various industries. These technologies converge to create a dynamic, interconnected environment where users can interact, transact, and collaborate seamlessly. Blockchain, in particular, serves as the backbone for secure, transparent, and decentralized transactions, while AI enhances user experiences through intelligent content generation and interaction personalization. The metaverse transcends traditional boundaries of space and time, ushering in new paradigms of social interaction, commerce, and entertainment. This shift towards a virtual-first world necessitates a reevaluation of regulatory frameworks and ethical considerations surrounding digital ownership, privacy, and security. As application development becomes increasingly intertwined with this immersive virtual realm, it is imperative for developers, technologists, and policymakers to collaborate in shaping a metaverse that is inclusive, secure, and conducive to innovation. This abstract serves as a starting point for deeper exploration into the intricacies of the metaverse that explores the critical aspects of the metaverse ecosystem and its pivotal role in enabling robust application development within this immersive digital realm.

articleTitle: Job-Profile Matching with CTN and MADRL with GEABB: A Recommender System
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Computer and Automation Engineering (ICCAE)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel approach to address the complex and challenging task of job-profile matching by enhancing the performance of the co-teaching network model, which is a state-of-the-art deep learning-based approach. Our approach involves implementing a self-adaptable algorithm that integrates an optimisation layer and adaptive building blocks. The proposed algorithm is trained and tested on a Kaggle data-set, and our numerical experiment demonstrates that the integration layer improved the accuracy of the co-teaching network by 5%, significantly enhancing the performance of the model in job-profile matching with real-world data. Our approach also incorporates self-adaptive building blocks that can adapt to changing environments and improve prediction accuracy, and the integration of multi-agent deep reinforcement learning, particle swarm optimisation, and grammatical evolution enhances the optimisation process and improves the accuracy of the model. Overall, our study presents a novel integration of adaptive building blocks and multi-agent deep reinforcement learning with the co-teaching network for job-profile matching and shows that our approach can significantly improve the performance of existing state-of-the-art models in this area.
